explanation: C++ supports both compile-time and runtime polymorphism.  Compile-time polymorphism, achieved through function overloading and templates, resolves function calls at compile time.  Runtime polymorphism, achieved through virtual functions and inheritance, resolves function calls at runtime based on the object's dynamic type. Understanding the difference is crucial for writing efficient and correct code.  Choosing the wrong type of polymorphism can lead to unexpected behavior or performance issues.
keywords: Static vs Dynamic Polymorphism, Compile time vs runtime polymorphism, C++ static dispatch, Virtual functions vs overloading
